targets.name: CHEVRON AUSTRALIA DOWNSTREAM HOLDINGS PTY LTD

merger_description:
ENEOS Holdings, Inc. via a wholly owned subsidiary (**ENEOS**), proposes to acquire 100% of the share capital of Chevron Australia Downstream Holdings Pty Ltd (**Chevron Australia Downstream**) (the **Acquisition**).

  

ENEOS Holdings is a Japanese petroleum and energy group. It operates five key business segments including petroleum products, oil and natural gas exploration and production, high performance materials, and electricity and renewable energy. In Australia, ENEOS’ relevant operations are focused on the downstream wholesale distribution of fuels and lubricants, with a nominal retail fuel footprint in rural New South Wales.

  

Chevron Corporation is a US based multinational integrated energy company. It operates two key business segments including the upstream exploration, development, and production of crude oil and natural gas and the downstream refining, marketing, transportation, and distribution of petroleum products, petrochemicals, lubricants, and additives.   


Chevron Australia Downstream encompasses Chevron’s integrated downstream platform that distributes fuels and lubricants across Australia and includes three Queensland based proprietary terminals and a national network of retail service stations operated by either the company or third-party retailers.

events.title: ENEOS – Chevron Australia Downstream - Phase 1 determination

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, submissions from third parties and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The Acquisition would lead to a very small increase in ENEOS’
share in the supply of secondary wholesale fuel and lubricants.
• The merged entity would likely continue to face competition
from multiple alternative suppliers of secondary wholesale fuel
and lubricants.
